newsitem.title: USA: Nassau County to refund $125 mln of bonds Aug 7.
newsitem.headline: Nassau County to refund $125 mln of bonds Aug 7.

text.p: Nassau County, N.Y., said Friday it planned to refund on Aug 7 around $125 million of bonds in order to capture the recent drop in fixed-income rates.
"You pick the best day and hope to ride the wave," said Daniel McCloy, deputy treasurer for the county. The negotiated deal will have two co-senior managers, Roosevelt & Cross and Smith Barney.
The county also plans to sell approximately $100 million of bonds in November, though that sale likely would be competitive. "That's a very rough figure," McCloy said.

While the November bond sale was expected to complete the long-term debt offerings for 1997, the county also expects to competitively sell around $55 million of bond anticipation notes on August 25. A mid-November sale of roughly $50 million of bond anticipation notes also was planned.

Nassau County's 1998 budget was scheduled to be approved by the legislature at the end of October. The county uses a calender year, and the 1997 pact totaled about $2.2 billion. "This one will probably be about the same amount," McCloy said.
